s: an award-recognised Śródmieście roaster-cafe with sidewalk seating under the trees
w: A bright, unfussy specialty cafe on Hoża street where the owner roasts the beans in-house -- precise espresso and rotating single-origin filter, with pavement tables that make it a natural stop between Śródmieście errands. One of two central Cophi locations that helped set the pace for Warsaw's specialty scene.
_facts: Located at Hoża 58/60, 00-682 Warszawa, Śródmieście
In-house roasted coffee, also branded Cafe Central Hoża / Cafelito
Sister location to Cophi Lwowska nearby
Sidewalk seating beneath street trees

s: the second Cophi roaster-cafe, opened to meet demand from the original Hoża spot
w: Opened as demand outgrew the original Hoża cafe, this second Cophi location keeps the same in-house-roasted, precisely brewed approach in a quieter corner of Śródmieście. Locals rotate between the two depending on which is on their way.
_facts: Located at Lwowska 2A, 00-614 Warszawa, Śródmieście
Second location of the Cophi (Cafe Central) roaster-cafe brand, opened 2020
Shares in-house roasting and menu approach with the Hoża original

s: the specialty cafe that helped put Warsaw on the third-wave coffee map
w: One of the shops that established Warsaw's specialty coffee scene, still drawing steady regulars on Marszałkowska for clean, well-sourced single-origin filter and knowledgeable, unhurried service. Less about spectacle than about a consistently good, honestly brewed cup.
_facts: Located at ul. Marszałkowska 27/35, 00-639 Warszawa
One of Warsaw's earlier, established specialty coffee shops
Known for single-origin filter coffee and knowledgeable baristas

s: a cosy, book-lined Żoliborz neighbourhood cafe away from the tourist centre
w: A relaxed, homely cafe in leafy Żoliborz, north of the centre, favoured by locals for its unhurried atmosphere, plants and shelves rather than any single showstopping brew. The kind of neighbourhood spot that rewards wandering beyond the historic core.
_facts: Located at Adama Mickiewicza 21, 01-517 Warszawa, Żoliborz
Neighbourhood cafe known for a cosy, plant-filled, unhurried atmosphere
Situated in Żoliborz, a residential district north of central Warsaw

s: the officially recognised smallest cafe in Poland, at six square metres
w: A coffee window so small -- 6 square metres, room for two seats inside -- that it holds an official Polish record for the country's smallest cafe. Started here in 2016 before growing into a small chain, but this original Puławska spot is still the one people mean when they say "the smallest cafe in Poland".
_facts: Located at Puławska 11, Mokotów, Warszawa
Certified by the Polish Records Society and Curiosities as Poland's smallest cafe, at 6 square metres
Trading at this address since 2016 as the original Dobro&Dobro location
Has since grown into a small chain of Dobro&Dobro cafes

s: a Michelin-starred kitchen blending Polish ingredients with chef Andrea Camastra's Italian-Asian instincts
w: Chef Andrea Camastra, Puglia-born and Oxford-trained in chemistry, runs an on-site lab alongside the kitchen to develop dishes that pull Polish produce through Italian and Asian technique. Held a Michelin star for four consecutive years running by 2026 -- confident, playful cooking on Plac Trzech Krzyży.
_facts: Located at Plac Trzech Krzyży 10/14, 00-499 Warszawa
Run by chef Andrea Camastra, who trained in chemistry at Oxford
Awarded a Michelin star for four consecutive years as of 2026
Blends Polish ingredients with Italian and Asian technique

s: a Michelin-starred Powiśle dining room run by chef Bartosz Szymczak
w: A small, precise modern-Polish restaurant in Powiśle, corner of Fabryczna and Rozbrat streets, run by chef and co-owner Bartosz Szymczak. Holds a Michelin star for ingredient-driven, technically careful cooking delivered without unnecessary formality.
_facts: Located at ul. Rozbrat 20, 00-447 Warszawa, Powiśle
Run by chef and co-owner Bartosz Szymczak
Holds a Michelin star, cited for modern Polish cuisine
Small, intimate dining room at the corner of Fabryczna and Rozbrat streets

s: chef Witek Iwański's tasting-menu restaurant channelling Praga's raw creative energy
w: A Michelin-recognised tasting-menu restaurant on Jagiellońska in Praga-Północ, run by chef Witek Iwański, that leans into the neighbourhood's unpolished, artistic identity rather than smoothing it over. Inventive plates built on Polish and international flavours, in a room that feels distinctly of its district.
_facts: Located at Jagiellońska 22/LU1, 03-719 Warszawa, Praga-Północ
Run by chef Witek Iwański, serving a tasting menu
Recognised in the Michelin Guide
Sited in Praga-Północ, Warsaw's traditionally working-class, increasingly creative district

s: restaurateur Mateusz Gessler's round-the-clock kitchen inside Hala Koszyki
w: One of restaurateur Mateusz Gessler's string of Warsaw dining rooms, set inside the restored Hala Koszyki market hall and serving long hours -- some sources describe it as effectively round-the-clock. Elevated, generous Polish and European plates in a space that borrows the hall's grand original architecture.
_facts: Located at Koszykowa 63, inside Hala Koszyki, Warszawa
Part of Mateusz Gessler's group of Warsaw restaurants
Known for long, sometimes round-the-clock opening hours
Set within the restored 1908 Hala Koszyki market hall
